quarterly_data.quarter: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Product mix: lithium-ion battery modules NT$2,441,954 thousand, 100% of 2025 revenue (2024: NT$1,981,355 thousand, 99%); others (power chargers, components and raw-material sales) NT$9,423 thousand. The modules serve three fields: battery backup unit / uninterruptible power system (BBU/UPS), power tools (PT) and light electric vehicles (LEV); the company describes itself as a midstream battery module maker (cell selection, safety protection circuit design and module assembly to customer requirements). Sales territories are mainly Europe and the United States, with direct and indirect export sales around 99% of revenue; in its sales-territory table, 2025 domestic sales were NT$1,382,855 thousand (56.41%) and export sales NT$1,068,522 thousand (43.59%), versus 2024 domestic NT$636,623 thousand (31.91%) and export NT$1,358,645 thousand (68.09%).
quarterly_data.figure: lithium-ion battery modules NT$2,441,954 thousand (100% of 2025 revenue); direct and indirect export around 99%

quarterly_data.quarter: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Management risk view: battery cells rely on Japan- and Korea-based suppliers, and with the rapid growth of lithium-ion battery energy storage applications (servers and data centers) cell supply will become tight, while Japanese and Korean cell makers face Chinese manufacturers' cost competitiveness. Responses: cell purchases are set from the year's shipments and major customers' forecasts; the company can draw on its world-renowned customers' group resources in quantity negotiations to guarantee cell supply; because of short supply of active components and battery cells it has prepared materials in advance (raising inventory risk) and signs agreements with customers to repurchase residual materials for certain products.

quarterly_data.quarter: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: 2026 outlook: the company expects the YoY growth of products such as lithium-ion battery backup modules for AI computing power centers to rise steadily, based on the industrial environment, market supply and demand, and its own production capacity and business development. Business plan: further expand its deployment in the AI industry while pursuing a balanced revenue ratio across battery backup modules, power-tool modules and light-electric-vehicle modules; management expects the battery backup systems industry to show impressive growth in the next few years and will develop new customers alongside existing ones.

quarterly_data.quarter: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Capex and capacity: no material capital expenditure in 2025 (property, plant and equipment rose 45.09% to NT$129,502 thousand, mainly from purchases of machinery and tooling); no plant-expansion plan as of the report date, and no investment confirmed for 2026 (to be evaluated against production capacity and business needs). Head office and plant in Kaohsiung; its subsidiary STL Energy Technology (S) Pte. Ltd. is the company's R&D center in Singapore. 2026 production policy: assembly of new lithium-ion batteries, more automated production, and readiness for customers' requirements for off-site production. 2026 cash projection: net cash flow from operating activities of NT$(510,532) thousand, primarily from building up inventory and raw materials to fulfill rising customer demand.
quarterly_data.figure: PP&E NT$129,502 thousand (+45.09%); projected 2026 operating cash flow NT$(510,532) thousand

quarterly_data.quarter: STL Technology annual report: 2025 Annual Report (05-27-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: R&D: 2025 R&D expense NT$93,492 thousand, 3.81% of revenue (2024: NT$80,329 thousand); 2026 R&D spending planned at about NT$106,249 thousand. Developed in 2025: lithium-ion battery backup modules for AI computing power centers, for server racks and for server motherboards, plus mass production of next-generation high-power-density power-tool modules and UAV modules. New products in development: ultra-high-voltage modules for AI computing power center lithium-ion BBU systems; lithium-ion BBU for high-power server systems; lithium-ion supercapacitor modules for high-power server power backup systems; modules for high-power UPS systems; next-generation ultra-high power density power-tool modules; modules for electric-assist bicycles, electric motorcycles and mobility scooters, agricultural UAVs and marine applications.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 R&D NT$93,492 thousand (3.81% of revenue); 2026 R&D about NT$106,249 thousand
